posts.title: How Generative AI is Changing Business Operations
posts.excerpt: From repetitive tasks to better customer experiences, explore where AI can make a practical difference.
body: The most useful AI projects begin with a clear business problem. Look for repetitive work where your team spends time searching, summarizing or drafting information, and define what a better outcome would look like.

A knowledge assistant can help a support team find the right answer faster. A document workflow can turn incoming information into structured drafts for review. In both cases, the aim is to give people more time for judgment and meaningful work.

Start with a focused pilot and measure quality, time saved and user feedback. Keep sensitive data protected, review generated outputs and make it easy for a person to take over when the system is uncertain.

posts.title: 10 Best Practices for Scalable Web Applications
posts.excerpt: A practical foundation for web products that grow alongside your business.
body: Scalability starts with clear boundaries. Separate presentation, business logic and persistence so each part can evolve independently. Define your API contracts and validate data at the edges.

Ten habits make a useful foundation: measure performance, define service boundaries, paginate large lists, index frequent queries, cache deliberately, move long tasks to a queue, validate inputs, automate critical tests, monitor errors and document operational procedures.
Avoid designing for hypothetical traffic before you understand real usage. Establish a baseline, find the bottleneck and improve the part of the system that is actually limiting your users.

posts.title: A Complete Guide to Deploying on Google Cloud
posts.excerpt: The key decisions behind a reliable cloud deployment, from configuration to monitoring.
body: Begin by identifying your application's runtime, storage needs and expected traffic. A containerized application is a portable starting point, but persistent data should live in storage that survives a deployment.

Keep configuration separate from application code. Store credentials in a secret manager, give each service only the access it needs, and use separate environments to validate changes before production.

A launch is only the beginning. Add health checks, centralized logs, error monitoring and a rollback process. Test how your application recovers from failure and make sure someone can understand the system when it needs attention.
